# sref: Siril truth harness for the stats package

`golden/siril_stats_golden.json` is produced by Siril's own code, compiled
from source. Nothing in it comes from the Go package.

## Siril source

- Siril 1.4.0 release tarball, https://free-astro.org/download/siril-1.4.0.tar.bz2
  (sha256 `439def7c40ad783afb82e87f3c656d85b449c701f67ab0a9b97ca372ea2d73c9`),
  unpacked at `/var/lib/aurbuild/pkgbuild/siril/src/siril-1.4.0`. GPL-3.0-or-later.
- The same functions are byte-identical in Siril git master
  `55111156048bf0fa86e9ca070208f5dadba3d184` (1.4.0-rc1-235, 2026-01-10).

Verbatim copies (checked by `make check-excerpt` and by the Go test
`TestGoldensReproduce/siril_excerpt_verbatim`):

| File | Siril function | Siril file |
|---|---|---|
| `rt_algo_excerpt.cc` | `findMinMaxPercentile` | `src/rt/rt_algo.cc` (sha256 `1716ffa0…8199`) |
| `siril_excerpt.c` (generated by `extract_siril.py`) | `siril_stats_float_sd`, `siril_stats_float_mad`, `reassign_to_non_null_data_float` | `src/algos/statistics_float.c` |
| | `sortnet_median_float` (+ its `sw` macro), `quickmedian_float`, `histogram_median_float` | `src/algos/sorting.c` |

Ours (no arithmetic that produces an expected value): `siril_stubs.h`
(threading forced to one thread, which gives the same integer histogram),
`siril_wrappers.c` (exports the file-static `reassign_to_non_null_data_float`),
and `sref.cc` (inputs, calls, JSON output). The float64 oracle for the Go
generic path is `rt_algo_excerpt.cc` included a second time with
`#define float double`.

## Build

- gcc/g++ 16.2.1 (20260810), x86-64.
- Flags: `-O3 -fno-math-errno -ffp-contract=off` — Siril's meson release
  build (`--buildtype release`, `arch_native` off, the default and what the
  Arch package uses). Building at `-O0` produces a byte-identical golden.
  A Siril built with `-Darch_native=true` (`-march=native`, which enables
  FMA contraction on FMA-capable CPUs) gives different results for 16 of
  the values; the Go code matches the default unfused build.

## Regenerate

    make -C stats/testdata/sref goldens

Re-running reproduces the committed file byte-for-byte
(`TestGoldensReproduce/sref` checks this when a compiler is available).

## Inputs

Inputs are written into the JSON (`input`, as float32/float64 IEEE bit
patterns in hex), except the large cases, which carry a `formula`
(a kind and an xorshift32 seed) that `siril_test.go` (`formulaData`,
`formulaData64`) regenerates with the same integer arithmetic:

- float32 (`formula()` in `sref.cc`): `uniform24` and `astro_u16` —
  random_10000, astro_u16_5000, f_astro_65537, f_uniform_16777219 (2^24+3),
  f_uniform_20000000, f_astro_20000000.
- generic path (`formula64()`): uint16_5000 (`u16`), float64_random_1000
  (`uniform53`), f_float64_uniform_70001 and f_float64_uniform_20000000
  (`uniform24`), f_uint16_adu_20000000 (`astro_adu`), int8_3000 (`i8`),
  uint32_3000 (`u32`), uint64_3000 (`u64`, half the values above 2^63),
  int64_wide_3000 (`i64`, up to 2^61), namedf32_5000 (`uniform24`, run in
  Go as a named type with underlying type float32).

Every formula value is an integer, or an integer times a power of two,
that the target type holds exactly, and the only floating-point
operations are exactly rounded ones, so C and Go produce the same values.

The 400 `small_*` cases (lengths 2..33) are `uniform24` formula inputs
too: one xorshift32 stream (`mixed_state(2024)`) gives each its length and
formula seed, and the seed is in the JSON.

The other generated inputs are written as a `gen` spec, not as values:
gradient_200, gradient_1000, with_zeros (`gradient`, `gradient_zero60`),
random_500, negative_301, with_nan_200 (`uniform`, `uniform_nan9`),
ties_1001 (`ties3`), adu_offset_1000 (`adu_quarter`) and, on the generic
path, int16_random_500, uint8_random_500, int32_negative_200, int64_100
(`ints`) and float64_offset_777 (`uniform`, float64). They come from
portable generators: xorshift32 from a hashed seed (`mixed_state`) and
exactly specified IEEE arithmetic (`gen_uniform`, `gen_gradient`,
`gen_ints`, `gen_f64`, ...), with no `std::*_distribution` (whose output
is implementation-defined), mirrored in Go by `genValues32` /
`genValues64` (each float operation rounded once by an explicit
conversion). Before round 2 they came from `std::mt19937` with
libstdc++'s distributions, so only libstdc++ reproduced the file.
Checked: clang++ 22.1.8 builds a harness that writes a byte-identical
golden (the Makefile's `CC=clang CXX=clang++`; clang warns about the
gcc-only `-Wno-maybe-uninitialized`).

Committed inputs (`input`): the cases of at most 100 values that are
edge cases in themselves (all_same, single, empty, n2..n10,
mixed_zero_nan, all_zero, float64_n2/n3/single/all_same).

Digests: every input that is not committed and has more than 64 values
(`DIGEST_MIN`) carries `in_sha256`, the sha256 of its IEEE bit patterns,
big-endian (float32 for the []float32 cases, the float64 values for the
generic ones). The Go test regenerates the input, checks the digest first
(a generator that does not mirror sref.cc fails there, by name) and then
every result bit for bit. For the same inputs the
reassign_to_non_null_data_float output is a count and sha256
(`nonnull_n`, `nonnull_sha256`), including the 2e7-element formula
inputs; committed inputs keep the explicit `nonnull` list. `sha256.h` is
ours (FIPS 180-4; it checks the "abc" vector before writing anything), and
its digests of the formerly committed inputs and non-null lists equal
Python `hashlib.sha256` of the hex values in the previous golden.

Format: one case per line, no whitespace inside a case.

Size: 813016 bytes before round 2; 444349 after the first formula inputs;
325722 with the `small_*` inputs no longer committed; 168634 with the
`gen` inputs, the digests and the compact format (every result value
unchanged).

`siril_test.go` (`requiredSirilF32`, `requiredSirilF64`) requires every
named case with its size and dtype, and exactly 424 float32 cases (400 of
them `small_*`): a regenerated golden that drops a case fails.
